description: Fixed eval set: 25 lesson topics typical of a first discrete math course (UCLA CS 61-style) and a first linear algebra course (MATH 33A-style). Do not edit between runs you want to compare.

topics.title: Propositional logic and truth tables
objectives: Define the connectives AND, OR, NOT and IMPLIES
Build a truth table for a compound proposition
Recognize a tautology from its truth table

topics.title: Why an implication with a false premise is true
objectives: State the truth table of p implies q
Explain vacuous truth with an everyday example
Distinguish an implication from its converse

topics.title: Proof by induction as a row of dominoes
objectives: Identify the base case and inductive step
Explain why the two steps cover every natural number
Prove that 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2

topics.title: Sets and Venn diagrams
objectives: Visualize union, intersection and complement
Apply De Morgan's laws to sets
Compute the size of a union with inclusion-exclusion for two sets

topics.title: Functions: injective, surjective, bijective
objectives: Draw a function as arrows between two sets
Classify a function as injective, surjective or bijective
Explain why a bijection means two sets have equal size

topics.title: The pigeonhole principle
objectives: State the pigeonhole principle
Apply it to show two people share a birthday month among 13
Use the generalized ceiling version

topics.title: Counting with permutations and combinations
objectives: Count ordered arrangements with n!/(n-k)!
Explain why combinations divide by k!
Compute C(5, 2) by listing and by formula

topics.title: Pascal's triangle and binomial coefficients
objectives: Build Pascal's triangle row by row
Connect entries to C(n, k)
Explain Pascal's rule C(n, k) = C(n-1, k-1) + C(n-1, k)

topics.title: Modular arithmetic as clock arithmetic
objectives: Compute remainders mod n
Visualize congruence classes on a circle
Add and multiply mod 12

topics.title: The Euclidean algorithm for gcd
objectives: Run the Euclidean algorithm on 48 and 18
Explain why gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b)
Visualize the algorithm as cutting rectangles into squares

topics.title: Graphs, degrees and the handshake lemma
objectives: Define vertices, edges and degree
Prove the sum of degrees equals twice the edges
Conclude the number of odd-degree vertices is even

topics.title: Trees and why they have n - 1 edges
objectives: Define a tree as a connected acyclic graph
Show adding an edge creates a cycle
Argue a tree on n vertices has n - 1 edges
prerequisites: Graphs, degrees and the handshake lemma

topics.title: Big-O notation and growth rates
objectives: Compare growth of n, n log n and n squared on one plot
State the definition of f = O(g)
Explain why constants are dropped

topics.title: Vectors as arrows and lists of numbers
objectives: Draw a 2D vector from its coordinates
Add vectors tip to tail
Scale a vector by a number

topics.title: Linear combinations and span
objectives: Form a linear combination of two vectors
Visualize the span of two vectors in the plane
Recognize when two vectors span only a line
prerequisites: Vectors as arrows and lists of numbers

topics.title: Matrices as linear transformations
objectives: Read a 2x2 matrix as where the basis vectors land
Animate a grid under a shear
Compute a matrix-vector product geometrically

topics.title: Matrix multiplication as composition
objectives: Apply a rotation then a shear
Explain why the order of multiplication matters
Compute the product of two 2x2 matrices

topics.title: The determinant as area scaling
objectives: Interpret the determinant as the area factor of the unit square
Compute ad - bc for a 2x2 matrix
Explain what a negative or zero determinant means

topics.title: Solving a 2x2 system as intersecting lines
objectives: Graph two linear equations
Identify the solution as the intersection point
Recognize no-solution and infinite-solution cases

topics.title: Inverse matrices as undoing a transformation
objectives: Describe the inverse as the transformation that undoes A
Compute the inverse of a 2x2 matrix
Explain why a zero determinant means no inverse

topics.title: Null space and column space
objectives: Define the column space as all outputs
Define the null space as inputs sent to zero
Visualize both for a rank-one 2x2 matrix

topics.title: Eigenvectors as directions that stay put
objectives: Find vectors that only stretch under a transformation
State Av = lambda v
Read eigenvalues as stretch factors

topics.title: The dot product and projection
objectives: Compute a dot product from coordinates
Interpret it as projection length times length
Use it to test for orthogonality
prerequisites: Vectors as arrows and lists of numbers

topics.title: Change of basis
objectives: Express one vector in two different bases
Build the change-of-basis matrix
Explain why the vector itself does not change

topics.title: Least squares as the closest point
objectives: Fit a line to three points that are not collinear
Explain the residuals as vertical distances
Connect least squares to orthogonal projection
